_meta: Refuter CALIBRATION harness (harness-first; the /refuters skill is deferred). Make a refuter's VALUE measurable and accept it like a review pass — with cited evidence (catch-rate / false-alarm vs the `default` baseline over seeded known-buggy/known-clean fixtures), not by assertion. ALIGNED WITH Anthropic's skill-creator eval methodology: the report is a `benchmark.json` matching skill-creator's schema (configuration = `with_skill` [the profile under test] / `without_skill` [the default baseline] — the exact strings its viewer needs; per-run `result` with pass_rate; `run_summary` with mean/stddev/min/max per configuration AND a NESTED `run_summary.delta` (the viewer reads delta from inside run_summary — a top-level delta is ignored); analyzer `notes`; and — because generate_review.py needs a runs-workspace (run dirs each with outputs/) and only feeds benchmark.json to its --benchmark TAB — the on-demand runner ALSO materializes that workspace, so it REUSES skill-creator's `generate_review.py` viewer instead of a bespoke one. Float formatting is pinned to ONE rounding convention so mean/stddev byte-match node≡python. Fold in its proven methodology: run each fixture N times and report mean±stddev (flag high-variance/flaky), a train/test HOLDOUT split to avoid overfitting the persona to the planted bugs, and a NON-DISCRIMINATING note when with_skill==without_skill on a fixture. Split like the rest of HeartBeat: (1) a DETERMINISTIC scorer (verdicts -> pass_rate + mean/stddev + Δ vs baseline, benchmark.json-shaped), suite-gated with STUB verdicts + node≡python parity; (2) `hb refuter-bench <name>` running a refuter over the fixtures via a STUB backend (deterministic) reusing the shared compose+refute dispatch, emitting benchmark.json; (3) an ON-DEMAND live tier (tests/refuter-calibrate.sh on local Ollama) that NEVER gates the suite, drives the real model N times, feeds generate_review.py, and supports --holdout, plus the measure-refuter-value.md how-to that flips the roadmap row. Design: planning/refuter-bench-scope.md. Determinism boundary: gate the plumbing (scoring, report schema, fixture labels, baseline delta, variance aggregation); the live model call is on-demand, never the gate.

phases.title: Calibration scorer + seeded fixtures (deterministic core, both runtimes)

tasks.title: Spec-first: author the scorer proof (catch / false-alarm / Δ-baseline, teeth) + fixture-distinctness
tasks.description: Author docs/howto/gate-examples/refuter-score.sh. MAIN (REFUTER-SCORE-OK): given fixtures each labelled expected∈{bug,clean} and a refuter's actual verdict∈{REFUTED,CLEAR} across N runs, assert the SCORER (harness plumbing, not refuter quality) computes per-configuration pass_rate (a bug fixture PASSES iff REFUTED, a clean fixture iff CLEAR → catch = pass_rate over bugs, false_alarm = 1 − pass_rate over cleans), aggregates over the N runs into mean/stddev/min/max, and Δ vs the baseline configuration — emitted in the EXACT skill-creator `benchmark.json` shape (configuration `with_skill`/`without_skill`, nested `result.pass_rate`, `run_summary.<cfg>.pass_rate.{mean,stddev,min,max}`, and `delta` NESTED as `run_summary.delta` — NOT a top-level sibling, which the viewer ignores); node ≡ python byte-identical on the SAME inputs with a pinned rounding convention. --selftest mutates the inputs — using HETEROGENEOUS per-run verdicts so stddev is non-zero (not vacuous), and at least one value whose 4-decimal rounding differs between banker's and half-away rounding (so the pinned convention is unambiguous, catching a node vs python float divergence) — so pass_rate, the mean/stddev variance aggregation, the delta VALUE, and its correct NESTED PATH are EACH individually load-bearing → SELFTEST-OK. --fixtures (FIXTURES-DISTINCT-OK): the buggy fixture is AUDITABLY distinct from its clean sibling — the clean phase enforces a guard (e.g. an authz check) that the buggy phase provably OMITS — so 'buggy' is a planted structural difference, not a bare manifest label; goes RED if the two are structurally identical. --selftest additionally proves the --fixtures teeth: making the buggy and clean fixtures identical makes --fixtures go RED. Drive both runtimes as the oracle. RED before cb2/cb3.

tasks.title: Implement the scorer in python AND node (parity, benchmark.json-shaped)
tasks.description: Add py/src/heartbeat/refuter_bench.py and its node twin plugin/templates/refuter_bench.js: `score(fixtures, runs)` -> per-configuration pass_rate (catch/false_alarm derived), `aggregate(runs)` -> {mean, stddev, min, max} over N runs (ONE pinned rounding convention, e.g. round to 4 decimals with a fixed string format, so python and node byte-match), `delta(with, without)`, and `build_report(...)` emitting the skill-creator `benchmark.json` shape (metadata.runs_per_configuration, runs[].{eval_id,eval_name,configuration,run_number,result}, run_summary.<cfg>, run_summary.delta [NESTED, not top-level], notes[] including a NON-DISCRIMINATING note when with==without and a HIGH-VARIANCE note when stddev is large). Pure functions over verdict lists — no dispatch/model. node and python return byte-identical output on the same input.

tasks.title: Seed calibration fixtures (known-buggy + known-clean) with declared expected verdicts
tasks.description: Create plugin/templates/refuter-fixtures/ with at least one KNOWN-BUGGY phase and one KNOWN-CLEAN phase that differ by a SINGLE, auditable planted difference — the clean phase enforces a guard (e.g. an authz check on a new path) that the buggy phase omits — so the 'buggy' label is backed by a structural fact refuter-score.sh --fixtures can verify, not an assertion. Add a manifest declaring each fixture's expected verdict (bug/clean); refuter-score.sh reads it so a mislabelled or missing fixture is caught. The fixtures are the ground truth the harness scores against; keep the planted difference minimal and obvious.

tasks.title: Wire the scorer proof + parity case + dev-tests + parity-notes
tasks.description: Add a Tnn group to tests/run-tests.sh running refuter-score.sh (marker same-line) + a --selftest check; add its row to docs/dev-tests.md. Add a tests/parity.sh case asserting the scorer returns identical numbers node ≡ python for a fixture verdict set. Record 'refuter score/calibration' as a shared surface in planning/parity-notes.md.

phases.title: `hb refuter-bench` command over the fixtures (deterministic via a stub, parity)

tasks.title: Spec-first: author the refuter-bench proof (shared-compose + miss-a-bug + unknown teeth)
tasks.description: Author docs/howto/gate-examples/refuter-bench.sh (prints REFUTER-BENCH-OK) driving the new `hb refuter-bench <name>` over the seeded fixtures with a STUB backend. CRITICAL (RB-2 fix): the stub is fixture-BLIND by construction — it keys its verdict on a MARKER that only the SHARED compose delivers (the profile persona + the base falsification checklist on its stdin), and echoes its received prompt so the proof asserts persona+checklist actually reached it. So `refuter-bench` cannot pass by re-implementing compose inline (drop the persona/checklist and the marker vanishes → verdicts flip → the assertion fails). Assert: one dispatch per fixture, scored via the CB scorer, and a --json report that is the skill-creator benchmark.json shape — its KEY-SET-AND-PATHS asserted HERE in RB against the real schema (metadata.runs_per_configuration, runs[].{eval_id,eval_name,configuration∈{with_skill,without_skill},run_number,result.pass_rate}, run_summary.<cfg>.pass_rate.{mean,stddev}, and delta at run_summary.delta — a top-level delta must FAIL this check) so skill-creator's generate_review.py --benchmark tab can consume it; a stub keyed to CLEAR the known-buggy fixture yields catch<1 (a blind refuter is distinguishable); an unknown refuter name errors non-zero; node ≡ python emit an identical report. --selftest proves the shared-compose, miss-a-bug, and unknown-name checks each load-bearing. RED before rb2.

tasks.title: Implement `hb refuter-bench <name> [--baseline <name>] [--json]` in python AND node
tasks.description: Add the command to py cli.py + node hb.js (parity). Resolve the profile (RS resolver), and for each fixture dispatch the refute using the SAME compose + refute dispatch the executor uses (hb refute-prompt / composePrompt), collect actual verdicts, score with refuter_bench (CB), and print the benchmark.json report (configuration `with_skill`=the profile); `--baseline <name>` scores a second refuter as configuration `without_skill` and reports the Δ + a non-discriminating note where they tie. Deterministic under a stub backend (HB_EXEC_CMD). Unknown profile errors (fail-closed).

tasks.title: Wire the refuter-bench proof + parity case + dev-tests
tasks.description: Add a Tnn group to tests/run-tests.sh running refuter-bench.sh (marker same-line) + --selftest; add its dev-tests.md row. Add a tests/parity.sh case asserting `hb refuter-bench` emits an identical report node ≡ python for a fixture set under a stub. Note refuter-bench in parity-notes.md.

phases.title: On-demand live tier (local Ollama, never gates) + the how-to (gated-docs)

tasks.title: Spec-first: author the on-demand live runner + a BEHAVIORAL --check with teeth
tasks.description: Author tests/refuter-calibrate.sh <name>: it drives a REAL local model (Ollama, no API key) to calibrate a refuter over the fixtures N times, emits the benchmark.json (RB) AND materializes the runs-workspace generate_review.py requires (run dirs each with outputs/), then opens the review via generate_review.py — gated behind model availability like tests/real-backend.sh, DELIBERATELY NOT referenced by tests/run-tests.sh (never gates). It supports `--holdout` via a DETERMINISTIC seeded split (train/test disjoint, covering all fixtures) so the split logic is checkable without a model. CD-2 fix: `--check` is BEHAVIORAL and SELF-CONTAINED (validates against a LOCAL copy of the required benchmark.json key-paths + runs-workspace layout — it must NOT import generate_review.py, since skill-creator may be absent): it reuses the RB path to validate the fixture manifest, the emitted benchmark.json paths (incl. nested run_summary.delta), the runs-workspace layout, and that the holdout split is deterministic+disjoint+total, WITHOUT calling a model — printing CALIBRATE-READY only when all validate. `--selftest` proves teeth: a removed/mislabelled fixture, a benchmark.json with delta at top-level instead of run_summary.delta, a missing runs-workspace outputs/ dir, or a non-disjoint holdout split each make --check go RED. RED before cd2.

Replace the '⬜ Not available yet' row for 'Test Whether Your Refuter Adds Value' in docs/howto/howto-list.md with a link to it. Every command real; claim only what the harness shows.

GATE_CB.desc: The deterministic SCORER (harness plumbing — NOT refuter quality) computes per-configuration pass_rate (catch/false-alarm), the mean/stddev/min/max variance aggregation over N runs, and Δ-vs-baseline from labelled fixtures + verdicts — emitted in the skill-creator benchmark.json shape, node ≡ python; and the seeded fixtures are auditably distinct (the buggy phase omits a guard the clean phase enforces) so their labels are grounded — proven with teeth, wired, parity-recorded.

review.prompt: Refute that CB is done. Does refuter-score.sh go RED without the scorer, and are pass_rate, the mean/stddev variance aggregation, AND the baseline-delta EACH individually load-bearing (a mutant that miscomputes one is caught)? Is the output the EXACT skill-creator benchmark.json shape — configuration with_skill/without_skill, nested result.pass_rate, run_summary.<cfg>.{mean,stddev}, and delta NESTED at run_summary.delta (a top-level delta would be silently ignored by the viewer — is that caught)? Is the mean/stddev rounding pinned so node and python byte-match (not vacuous under stubs — does cbb use heterogeneous per-run verdicts so stddev≠0)? Do node and python return byte-identical output on the same verdict set (real parity)? Crucially: does --fixtures prove the buggy fixture is STRUCTURALLY distinct from the clean one (a planted omission the check can see), so 'buggy' is not a bare label — RED if identical? Do the gate strings avoid implying this deterministic tier measures refuter VALUE (it scores the harness; real value is the on-demand live tier)? Is the shared surface recorded in parity-notes? End SOUND or UNSOUND.
